record.reason: Training-only target scaling fits training returns much more closely but fails the preregistered cross-period ranking and long-short screen. Squared-error compression does not establish out-of-sample predictive gain.

findings: Both windows lose aggregate gross long-short return; second-window RankIC also declines. Three of four registered primary comparisons fail the nonnegative screening gate.
Both windows have worse observed worst-day returns and higher turnover. First-window MSE rises while second-window MSE falls; neither raw loss nor ranking alone passes the required trade-off.
The frozen weighting formula behaves as configured: opening target-variance emphasis proxy falls from about38.81 to13.27 percent and40.41 to13.28 percent. This is not a gradient measurement.

Opening effects are mixed: first-window opening long-short falls from+3.142bp to-0.710bp and its worst opening day deteriorates; second-window opening long-short improves from-1.026bp to+2.501bp, but the remaining seven-time long-short deteriorates by0.894bp. Reduced opening emphasis is not a consistent validation improvement.
limitations: One seed, two four-day research windows and repeated exploratory comparisons; no evidence of official score or robust out-of-period gains.

Per-time target variance is not conditional noise variance and the logs contain no per-time gradients.

risk_notes: Both windows improve point RankIC and gross long-short, but the first-window long-short interval and second-window RankIC interval cross zero. The small observed increments require seed replication.

Observed worst-day long-short falls in both windows, by about0.408 and0.577bp; turnover rises in both windows. Candidate daily long-short remains positive on these eight dates, which does not establish safety outside them.

First-window opening long-short falls from+3.142 to-1.255bp and opening RankIC falls; most first-window improvement is in the other seven times. Second-window opening long-short improves slightly but remains negative, and its worst opening day deteriorates.

Only one seed and eight research dates, with prior selection on the same windows. This is a screening lead, not a proven competition improvement.

The complete grid has a positive average RankIC difference, but seed29 in July18-21 loses long-short return and seed47 in July25-28 loses RankIC. The per-seed two-window primary gate fails; an average cannot override these failures.

Pooled RankIC delta is about +0.004339, with a two-day-block interval above zero. Pooled gross long-short delta is about +0.3603bp, but its interval crosses zero. These retain a representation research lead, not an adoption conclusion.

Worst-day gross long-short deteriorates in three of six pairs; the largest drop is about 2.0092bp in July18-21 seed29. Turnover rises in five of six pairs, RankIC IR falls in four, and the short-window long-short Sharpe estimate falls in five. Four-day annualized Sharpe estimates are descriptive and unstable.

All three first-window seeds lose opening RankIC; opening long-short falls for seed11 and seed29. First-window seed29 worst opening return moves from about -0.9322bp to -14.3561bp. Second-window opening means improve, but opening tail losses persist. Absolute section metrics are retained to avoid interpreting a smaller opening share as a universal improvement.

First-window MSE worsens for all three seeds, while second-window MSE improves for all three. Aggregate MSE is essentially flat; second-window validation MSE remains above the training-mean constant reference for all three candidates.
All candidate runs stay within recorded local limits; peak RSS is about 5970.5MiB, close to the 6144MiB cap. No full-range runtime or official platform acceptance is inferred.

Only eight distinct research dates and three seeds are available. These windows already informed earlier choices; selection bias and weak short-block uncertainty limit generalization. All returns are local gross approximations and do not include official transaction-cost treatment.

findings: Turnover falls in all six pairs, but every first-window seed loses RankIC and gross long-short return. Second-window seed47 also loses gross long-short.
Observed worst-day long-short return worsens in all six pairs. Lower turnover alone does not satisfy the registered preservation and risk requirements.

limitations: Only eight distinct validation days and repeated exploratory model selection. Seed averaging does not create independent dates.
Turnover includes overnight transitions and returns are local gross approximations; no fee/slippage-calibrated trade-off justifies accepting the quality loss.
Offline recomputation used the frozen phase3c raw12/all8/train_std/none-weight source, independent of pending book/trade outcomes. No optimizer updates or final-check views occurred.

findings: The registered same-width trade-information screen fails three of four primary comparisons: RankIC falls in both windows; long-short falls in July18-21 and rises in July25-28. Do not expand seeds or adopt log1p based on pooled return alone.

Pooled RankIC delta is about -0.0055003 and gross long-short delta is about +0.0847bp; both short-block intervals cross zero. Turnover rises in both windows, with pooled delta about +0.05060 and an interval wholly above zero.

Opening RankIC and gross long-short improve in both windows relative to zero15, but other-seven-time RankIC falls in both. First-window other-seven gross long-short loses about 0.5488bp. Opening improvement does not rescue the full-time ranking screen.
Observed worst-day gross long-short improves in July18-21 and deteriorates in July25-28. The second-window worst opening return remains about -13.3712bp despite improving from the zero15 control.

MSE improves in the first window and worsens in the second. Training and inference used original12 LOB eligibility for both 15-dimensional arms; exact key/target and data/source/environment checks pass.

A separate raw12 reference shows a positive pooled gross-return difference but a second-window RankIC decline. The 12-to-15 input and normalization/architecture change prevents attributing that comparison to trade information. The same-width control is the relevant test of incremental trade activity.
limitations: One seed and eight distinct research dates only; failure screening prevents the preregistered 29/47 expansion. This does not prove trade information is universally unhelpful.
Both arms use 1500 updates with batch32, approximately 48000 sample exposures and 0.6009/0.6006 epoch of the ten-date all-eight-time pool. The user chose no additional full12 expanded-data training.
These research windows have been reused for selection. Gross local metrics omit official costs/slippage, and neither final-check data nor official platform performance is assessed.

findings: Compared with the fixed raw12 seed11 reference, log1p15 improves first-window RankIC and gross long-short, but second-window RankIC declines while gross long-short rises. Thus the actual recipe is not uniformly better across both primary metrics.

Pooled gross long-short difference is about +0.5281bp with a two-day-block interval above zero, while pooled RankIC difference about +0.0028569 has an interval crossing zero. These are descriptive results from one seed and eight reused research dates.

First-window worst-day return and turnover improve; second-window worst-day return and turnover deteriorate. Opening gross-return means and worst-opening-day values improve in both windows, but second-window opening RankIC is worse and its worst opening day remains negative.

The input changes from12 LOB channels to15 channels including log1p(volume, canonical-yuan amount, deal_number), and therefore changes normalization/model dimensionality. Archived adapter.py and package.py also differ due to the tested memory and package-dependency patches. Exact config/source differences are listed; this is not a single-factor feature comparison.

In the actual same-width zero15-versus-log1p15 experiment, RankIC declines in both windows and first-window long-short declines. A favorable raw12 comparison therefore cannot establish useful incremental trade information or override the failed registered screen.
limitations: No causal attribution to individual inputs, architecture, normalization or source changes.
Reference and candidate share evaluation settings, exact full/scored prediction keys/targets, data-file identity, environment, 1500 actual updates and batch32, but each arm has only one seed here.
